question: Morgan Stanley Associate - Software Engineering (Java) technical round 2 (offline). One task was to **write a complete service on paper following the layers Controller to Service to DAO to Entity**. Expect to write classes in Java (likely Spring-style), keep layers separate and discuss validation, errors and transactions.
lookingFor: Correct separation of layers and responsibilities.
Clean, compilable Java written without an IDE.
Error handling, validation and transaction boundaries.
followUps: Why should the transaction boundary be in the service layer?
Why use DTOs instead of returning entities?
How would you unit test the service without a database?
How do you handle exceptions across layers consistently?
What changes if you use JDBC instead of JPA in the DAO?
